### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via bootstrapDeclaredCapabilities (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx`  _(via bootstrapDeclaredCapabilities (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permissions-matrix.mdx`  _(via ownedBy (symbol, a field of interface CapabilityNameCollisionDiagnostic))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx`  _(via ownedBy (symbol, a field of interface CapabilityNameCollisionDiagnostic))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx`  _(via ownedBy (symbol, a field of interface CapabilityNameCollisionDiagnostic))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ownedBy (symbol, a field of interface CapabilityNameCollisionDiagnostic))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b3d6918b86abcc31f82e963d2fabc37308bc4bb7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2d6efa6fa32bfc85809754d0e7e3a4f5afae9929` — the merge of head `9cbca2136fde1f610cd7d1f28f77ae5afe9b0852` into base `b3d6918b86abcc31f82e963d2fabc37308bc4bb7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2d6efa6fa32bfc85809754d0e7e3a4f5afae9929 && git checkout 2d6efa6fa32bfc85809754d0e7e3a4f5afae9929
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b3d6918b86abcc31f82e963d2fabc37308bc4bb7 9cbca2136fde1f610cd7d1f28f77ae5afe9b0852 && git checkout -B drift-repro b3d6918b86abcc31f82e963d2fabc37308bc4bb7 && git merge --no-ff 9cbca2136fde1f610cd7d1f28f77ae5afe9b0852

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b3d6918b86abcc31f82e963d2fabc37308bc4bb7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b3d6918b86abcc31f82e963d2fabc37308bc4bb7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `claude-fable-5-1`

Reviewed head: `9cbca2136fde1f610cd7d1f28f77ae5afe9b0852` (PR #18088, card #18023, base `b3d6918b8`). Independent at-tier review; the PR body was treated as the claim under test, not as evidence. Everything below was re-measured in a fresh checkout of the head: `pnpm install`, closure build, the full package suite, the dist probe, and the ablation.

### ① Derived judgments — acceptance set and public surface, item by item

| Item | PR's claim | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Foreign-owner refusal reaches the author with no logger passed | 0 → 1 console line, `skippedForeign` unchanged at 1 | **Right.** Pinned in `bootstrap-declared-capabilities.test.ts` (no-logger case, all five console channels spied); the skip, the untouched foreign row and `materializedNames` are asserted unchanged in the same case. |
| Own diagnostic record type + own key on the seeder outcome | `CapabilityNameCollisionDiagnostic`, `CapabilitySeedOutcome.collisions?` (absent, never `[]`) | **Right.** The absent-not-empty invariant is pinned by the silence control. |
| Reuse of the shared predicate, no re-derivation | seeder branch now calls `permissionSetNameIsForeign` instead of `===` | **Right.** Read the predicate: `(owner ?? null) !== (declarer ?? null)`. For a string owner this is identical to the old `===`; for a nullish owner both the old and the new form read FOREIGN, so the skip behaviour is preserved by construction, and the PR pins that row shape. |
| `permissionSetNameCollisionDiagnostic` / `format…` / `report…` deliberately not reused | consequence differs; sink discipline restated | **Right.** `reportPermissionSetNameCollisions` is typed on `readonly PermissionSetNameCollisionDiagnostic[]` and words "permissions are NOT in effect"; the capability record words "the name still resolves". The restated discipline (no-sink prints, injected sink preferred, receiver kept, empty pass silent) is four pins, all present in `capability-name-collision.test.ts`. |
| New exported symbols reachable from the published entry | four values + one type, probed on `dist/index.{d.ts,js,mjs}` | **Right, and the probe discriminates.** `package.json` publishes only `exports["."]` → `dist/index.*`, `files` includes `dist`; `src/index.ts` re-exports them by name (no `export *` anywhere in that file). My rebuild reproduces the PR's counts exactly for the four values and both controls (positive `permissionSetNameIsForeign` 4/5/4, negative `nonexistentSymbolXyz18023` 0/0/0). A runtime import of both `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.mjs` returns `string`/`function` for all four values and `undefined` for the negative control. |
| `CapabilitySeedOutcome.collisions` is NOT what decides `yes` | the seeder is not re-exported | **Right.** `bootstrapDeclaredCapabilities` is `undefined` on both built entries, and `CapabilitySeedOutcome` has 0 hits in `dist/index.d.ts`. So the new key is not a key on a published payload; the `yes` rests on the `index.ts` re-exports alone, exactly as the PR says. |
| Reverse verification turns red for the right reasons | 4 failed / 39 passed under the mutation | **Right.** I reproduced the mutation from the committed state: HEAD blob `3cb4ec4a3…` → mutated `0b2ec0f47…` (same hashes the PR reports), anchors 1/0 → 0/1. Running the three affected files: the same four seeder pins redden, and additionally both repurposed `bootstrap-seed-round-trips` cases redden (6 failed / 79 passed over 85), while the no-collision silence control and every pure-function pin stay green. Restore verified by blob hash and a clean `git status`. |
| No test skipped, disabled, quarantined or weakened | — | **Right.** No `.skip`/`.only`/`.todo` added and no `it(`/`describe(` line removed anywhere in the diff. |
| The two repurposed round-trip cases are strictly stronger | prose match → token match + record assertion | **Right.** Each case keeps every prior assertion (`skippedForeign`, untouched `package_id`, `materializedNames`, a warn line present) and adds the outcome record. The ablation proves the new token assertion is itself discriminating: both cases redden under it. |

One precision remark that does not change the reading: the PR's `CapabilityNameCollisionDiagnostic (type)` row of 5/3/2 is a substring artefact. With word boundaries the type reads 5/0/0, because the 3 and 2 in the JS files are hits inside `formatCapabilityNameCollisionDiagnostic`. A type living only in the `.d.ts` is the correct shape, and the `types` condition of the published entry reaches it, so the symbol is genuinely published.

Head-state facts: full package suite on this head is 113 files / 2181 tests passing in my run; `node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 18088` exits 0; all 38 check runs on the head are success or skipped; production still injects `ctx.logger` at `security-plugin.ts`, so the `console.warn` fallback changes only sink-less direct callers.

### ② Semver grading

Declared `@objectstack/plugin-security: minor`. The diff adds four value exports and one type export on the sole published entry, plus an optional key on an unpublished outcome type; nothing is removed or renamed and no wire byte moves. That is additive public surface, which is `minor`. Level and changeset **agree**; the `patch`-under-`yes` refusal (#16361) is not triggered.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `permissionSetNameIsForeign` keeps its axis-bearing name while now serving both axes — **accepted**. The predicate's signature and docblock are already axis-independent; renaming a published export is a breaking change outside this card's scope, and the import site documents the choice. Not escalated.
- `reportPermissionSetNameCollisions` not generalised — **accepted**. Verified by reading it: its record type and its sentence are permission-set-specific. Threading an axis through it would make one function state two consequences. The two lines of sink discipline that are duplicated are pinned on both axes independently, which is the right price.
- `sys_capability.scope` reader survey — **accepted as the bounded observation it claims to be**. My own grep finds no non-test reader of a `scope` column adjacent to a `sys_capability` read. Note that the PR's list of "readers" is narrower than the set of files that merely name the table (spec constants, `plugin-sharing` provenance, `runtime/app-plugin.ts` also name it); the operative claim, that none reads `scope` for an authorization decision, holds on the head, and the record's `severity` docblock already routes any future over-grant path to its own card. Not escalated.
- `cleanupPackagePermissions` coverage — **accepted**. Verified: it touches `sys_permission_set`, `sys_position_permission_set` and `sys_user_permission_set` only, so the diagnostic is right not to promise a disappearing row. A capability-uninstall change is an ADR-0086 D3 card of its own, not this one's.
- The remaining doubly-optional refusal sites (five, listed in the dev report on the card) — **escalated to the PM seat for triage filing**, as the report already does; it is the same defect class one branch over and correctly not ridden in here.
